# Repositories {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 3 &middot; PART A]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

[A repository is a directory of tarballs with an index file.]{.subhead}


## What is a repository

`install.packages()` downloads from the repositories in
`getOption("repos")`.

A repository is a base URL with a fixed directory layout. It can be a CRAN
mirror, Posit Package Manager, a local directory (`file://`), or any server that
serves that layout
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Setting-up-a-package-repository)).

```bash
R -q --no-echo -e 'getOption("repos")'
```

## Repository layout

```text
<repo>/
  src/contrib/
    PACKAGES              <- the index, plain text, DCF format
    PACKAGES.gz
    PACKAGES.rds
    R6_2.6.1.tar.gz
    xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz
    ...
    Archive/              <- CRAN's convention, not part of the format
```

R downloads the index, then the tarballs it needs. We build a repository in
block 6.

## The `PACKAGES` index

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

[cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES)

```text
Package: a5R
Version: 0.6.0
Depends: R (>= 4.2)
Imports: cli, rlang (>= 1.1.0), units, vctrs (>= 0.6.0), wk (>= 0.9.0)
Suggests: arrow, knitr, pillar, rmarkdown, sf, terra, testthat (>=
        3.0.0), tibble, withr
License: Apache License (>= 2)
MD5sum: ab65526f7628cd1862afe47209fa546b
NeedsCompilation: yes
Published: 2026-09-08 11:50:15 UTC
```

DCF format: `Field: value`, continuation lines indented, a blank line between
records, the same format as `DESCRIPTION`.

The plain file is about 7&nbsp;MB. R downloads `PACKAGES.rds` first, and
falls back to `PACKAGES.gz` and `PACKAGES`
([packages.R](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/library/utils/R/packages.R)).

## What CRAN checks, and what it doesn't

About 25,000 packages, maintained by a volunteer CRAN team
([CRAN policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html)).

CRAN requires:

- The package passes `R CMD check`
- Strong dependencies come from CRAN or Bioconductor
- A licence that lets CRAN distribute it
- Source for all components, for open-source licences

The CRAN team can remove or modify packages without notice.

What goes into your site library is your decision.

## CRAN keeps one version; older ones are archived

`src/contrib/` holds the current version of each package. Older versions
move to `src/contrib/Archive/<pkg>/` and stay there
([CRAN policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html)).

[cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/xml2/](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/xml2/)

```text
...
xml2_1.3.8.tar.gz    2025-03-14   149K
xml2_1.4.0.tar.gz    2025-08-20   150K
xml2_1.4.1.tar.gz    2025-10-27   150K
xml2_1.5.0.tar.gz    2025-11-17   151K
xml2_1.5.1.tar.gz    2025-12-01   151K
xml2_1.5.2.tar.gz    2026-01-17   151K
```

::: {.note}
[Not reproducible]{.note-label}
`install.packages("xml2")` installs whatever is current. Archived versions
are not in `PACKAGES`, so R cannot resolve against them. Use the tarball
URL, a snapshot repository, `remotes::install_version()` or `renv`.
:::

## Packages removed from CRAN

CRAN archives packages whose check errors are not fixed, for example after
a new R x.y.0 release
([CRAN policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html)). An
archived package leaves `PACKAGES`.

```r
# is anything we depend on already gone?
db <- available.packages()
ours <- c("R6", "xml2", "somepkg")
setdiff(ours, rownames(db))
```

A local copy of every tarball you depend on protects you from this. We
build one in block 6.

## `available.packages()`

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
ap <- available.packages()
nrow(ap)
colnames(ap)
```

```text
[1] 25121

 [1] "Package"               "Version"               "Priority"             
 [4] "Depends"               "Imports"               "LinkingTo"            
 [7] "Suggests"              "Enhances"              "License"              
[10] "License_is_FOSS"       "License_restricts_use" "OS_type"              
[13] "Archs"                 "MD5sum"                "NeedsCompilation"     
[16] "File"                  "Published"             "Built"                
[19] "Repository"           
```

```r
ap["xml2", c("Version", "Imports", "NeedsCompilation")]
```

```text
                         Version                          Imports
                         "1.6.0" "cli, methods, rlang (>= 1.1.0)"
                NeedsCompilation
                           "yes"
```

## `PACKAGES` has no `SystemRequirements`

```r
ap["xml2", "SystemRequirements"]
```

```text
Error in ap["xml2", "SystemRequirements"] : subscript out of bounds
```

CRAN's `PACKAGES` does not carry the field, so R cannot tell from the index
which OS libraries a package needs. 

`tools::CRAN_package_db()` reads a different file, CRAN's
`web/packages/packages.rds`, with most `DESCRIPTION` fields of the current
CRAN packages
([`?CRAN_package_db`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/tools/html/CRANtools.html)):

```r
db <- tools::CRAN_package_db()
db[db$Package == "xml2", "SystemRequirements"]
```

```text
[1] "libxml2: libxml2-dev (deb), libxml2-devel (rpm)"
```

It covers CRAN only.

## Querying the index

```r
ap <- available.packages()

# everything that needs a compiler
sum(ap[, "NeedsCompilation"] == "yes")

# published in the last week
recent <- ap[as.Date(ap[, "Published"]) > Sys.Date() - 7, "Package"]
length(recent)

# packages with a licence we cannot accept
ap[ap[, "License"] == "AGPL-3", "Package"]
```

The default filters drop packages for another R version, another OS, or a
sub-architecture, and keep only the latest version of each package.
`filters = character()` turns them off
([`?available.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/available.packages.html)).

## CRAN check results

CRAN checks every package on 13 platform "flavors"
([CRAN check flavors](https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html)).

[cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_xml2.html](https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_xml2.html)

| Flavor | Platform |
|---|---|
| `r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-gcc` | R-devel, Debian, gcc |
| `r-devel-linux-x86_64-fedora-clang` | R-devel, Fedora, clang |
| `r-release-macos-arm64` | Current R, macOS arm64 |
| `r-release-windows-x86_64` | Current R, Windows |
| `r-oldrel-*` | Previous R |

Read this page before you add a package to your site library.

## CRAN checks reverse dependencies

```r
rd <- tools::package_dependencies("xml2", db = ap,
                                  reverse = TRUE, which = "most")
lengths(rd)
```

```text
xml2
 688
```

Before submitting an update, a maintainer is expected to check the packages
that depend on it. If the API changes, the affected maintainers get at least
two weeks' notice
([CRAN policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html)).

::: {.note}
[In your own library]{.note-label}
Upgrading one package can break the packages that depend on it. Test the
package set together.
:::

## Binary packages

CRAN builds Windows and macOS binaries of the latest version of each
package, for the current R and often for the previous one and R-devel. They must not depend on specific versions
of external software
([CRAN policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html)).

```text
src/contrib/                                  <- source, all platforms
bin/windows/contrib/4.6/                      <- Windows, R 4.6
bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.6/          <- macOS arm64, R 4.6
```

A binary package is an installed package in an archive. Installing it needs
no compiler.

On Windows and macOS, CRAN packages must link external libraries
statically, so the binaries need no system libraries at run time.

## No CRAN binaries for Linux

Linux binaries link against the shared libraries of one distribution
release. Posit Package Manager builds them per distribution
([Package Manager docs](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/serving-binaries.html)):

```text
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/latest
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/rhel9/latest
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/4.6
```

The `__linux__/<distro>` form reads the R version and architecture from R's
user agent. The `bin/linux/` form puts them in the URL.

## Dated snapshots

Package Manager serves CRAN as it was on a given date
([Package Manager docs](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/repositories.html)):

```text
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2026-06-01
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/2026-06-01
```

Against a snapshot, `install.packages("dplyr")` gets the same version every
time, without pinning versions yourself.

```r
options(repos = c(
  CRAN = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2026-06-01"
))
```

## Multiple repositories

`repos` is a named character vector. If a package is in more than one
repository, R takes the **highest version**, and the first-named repository
only on a tie
([`?available.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/available.packages.html)).

```r
options(repos = c(
  INTERNAL = "https://pkgs.example.com/prod",
  CRAN     = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2026-06-01"
))
```

An internal build overrides CRAN only if its version is at least as high.

```r
# where would this actually come from?
ap <- available.packages()
ap["dplyr", c("Version", "Repository")]
```

::: {.note}
[Diagnostic]{.note-label}
When a user reports an unexpected version, check the `Repository` column.
:::
